why: Lucian wants short, dash-led burst trades that snowball the lane before the enemy carry scales. Lulu denies that window directly: Polymorph interrupts Lucian mid-dash, her shield absorbs the combo that follows, and Glitterlance slows his re-engage. Teams picked Lulu after Lucian at 1.78x her base rate across 20 games (55% wins), because she also scales into a second protective layer for her own carry in teamfights.
tips: Hold Polymorph for Lucian's dash forward instead of using it to poke, so his trade has no follow-through.
Pair Lulu with a hypercarry who uses the attack-speed steroid and Wild Growth well, such as Kog'Maw, Jinx or Yunara.
Play the lane to survive to two items rather than contesting Lucian's level-two all-in.

why: Lucian's lane strength depends on dashing in, bursting, and dashing out before he can be punished. Rakan removes the safe exit: Grand Entrance knocks him up as he commits, and The Quickness plus Battle Dance let Rakan re-engage or peel repeatedly. The pick spiked to 2.6x its base rate after Lucian across 19 games and won 68.4% of them, the strongest Lucian answer in the set.
tips: Start the trade as Lucian dashes in, not before, so he cannot use the second dash to leave the knock-up.
Pair Rakan with Xayah whenever she is open, since the duo's shared all-in is what usually kills Lucian before he resets.
Keep Rakan's engage available when Lucian has ultimate up, because interrupting The Culling early wins the extended trade.

why: Lucian with Milio is a lane that bursts, then disengages for free behind Milio's shields and kick. Xayah and Rakan attack both halves of that plan: Rakan engages before Milio can peel, and Xayah's feather recall roots whichever target Rakan lifts, while Featherstorm gives Xayah an untargetable answer to Lucian's ultimate. Teams reached for the duo at 3.51x base rate after seeing Lucian and Milio, winning 73.3% of 15 games.
tips: Draft Xayah and Rakan together on the same rotation after Lucian and Milio show, before either half can be banned away.
Set feathers behind Lucian before Rakan goes in, so the recall root lands during the knock-up.
Force fights while Milio's kick is on cooldown, because without it Lucian has no clean exit from the all-in.

why: Into Lucian and Milio's burst-and-disengage lane, Yunara and Lulu trade protection for a longer fight. Lulu's Polymorph and shield blunt Lucian's opening combo, and once that window passes Yunara's Cultivation of Spirit attack-speed steroid wins the extended auto-attack trade that Lucian cannot sustain. Teams picked the pair at 1.86x base rate in 15 games, splitting them almost evenly at 53.3% wins.
tips: Give the first push to Lucian and Milio and farm under tower until Lulu has Polymorph and shield both available.
Save Wild Growth for Yunara when Lucian commits his ultimate, so she can keep attacking through it.
Pair the lane with a frontline jungler who buys Yunara time to stack attacks in teamfights.

why: Ashe's draft value is the Enchanted Crystal Arrow: a long-range pick tool that starts fights her team chooses. Milio answers it without needing to out-range her, because Breath of Life cleanses the arrow's stun off his carry and resets the fight Ashe just started. He was picked at 1.67x base rate after Ashe in 14 games (57.1% wins), and his shields also soften Ashe's perma-slow poke lane.
tips: Hold Milio's ultimate for the arrow in teamfights instead of spending it on poke damage.
Pair Milio with an immobile carry who gains the most from a cleanse, such as Aphelios or Jinx.
Stand the carry behind frontline so an arrow forces Milio's ultimate only when the follow-up dive is also coming.

why: Yunara wins fights by stacking attacks inside her Cultivation of Spirit window and finishing with Transcend One's Self, so the target has to survive one long, high-speed trade. Milio extends exactly that survival: layered shields, a disengage kick, and a cleanse keep his carry alive past Yunara's steroid window. Teams still reached for him at 1.53x base rate after Yunara, though the pick only won 42.9% of 14 games, so the protection alone does not carry the matchup.
tips: Pair Milio with a carry who out-ranges Yunara or can disengage with her own dash, not a stationary turret.
Use the kick the moment Yunara activates her attack-speed steroid, to burn its short duration.
Avoid grouping in a line for Yunara's beam, and scatter until her ultimate window ends.

why: Yunara's all-in commits her to standing and attacking at high speed, which makes her dive predictable. Renata Glasc punishes committed dives: Bailout keeps the dive target fighting through Yunara's burst, and Hostile Takeover turns Yunara's own attack speed against her team if she stays in range. Teams picked Renata at 1.96x base rate after Yunara and won 66.7% of 12 games.
tips: Cast Bailout on the teammate Yunara is focusing, early enough that the takedown reset can trigger.
Pair Renata with a carry who keeps attacking while bailed out, such as Kalista or Samira.
Hold Hostile Takeover until Yunara's team groups to follow her in, rather than firing it at her alone.

why: Locke is a melee magic-damage diver who sticks with slows and a resetting dash, then executes low targets with his totem. K'Sante survives that pattern better than most frontliners: he soaks the opening burst, then uses All Out to drag Locke away from the carry Locke marked. Teams picked K'Sante at 1.85x base rate after Locke across 12 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Save K'Sante's ultimate to pull Locke away from his execute target, not to start fights.
Build magic resistance early, since Locke's damage is magic despite his melee range.
Keep the carry away from Locke's totem area so the execute marks land on the frontline instead.

why: Cassiopeia wants a static, poisoned front-to-back fight where she can twin-fang one target down. Gnar disrupts that shape from a different lane: he arrives with Mega Gnar's area stun, and in Mini form he out-ranges her poison zone while building rage safely. Teams picked him at 1.93x base rate after Cassiopeia, but won only 41.7% of 12 games, so the draft logic has not yet converted into results.
tips: Time Mega Gnar's arrival to objective setups, where Cassiopeia must stand in her poison and fight.
Keep Gnar's rage near full before teleporting, so he lands as Mega rather than charging it in the fight.
Pair Gnar with a mid laner who can follow his wall stun with burst before Cassiopeia repositions.

why: Nocturne's Paranoia dive lands on a chosen target with a fear tether that punishes anyone who runs. Renekton is built to stand in that dive: his empowered stun is point-and-click, holds Nocturne through the fear, and his ultimate health pool survives the opening burst. Teams reached for him at 2.74x base rate after Nocturne, the highest lift in this group, though he won only 33.3% of 12 games, so pro teams value the tool more than the results so far support.
tips: Keep Renekton near the carry Nocturne is most likely to dive, instead of splitting him to a side lane at ultimate timings.
Spend the empowered stun on Nocturne the moment he lands, before his fear tether completes.
Pair Renekton with a support who can shield the dive target through the first second of Paranoia.

why: Vi locks one carry with Vault Breaker and her ultimate, and her team collapses on that target. Galio answers from across the map: Hero's Entrance lands on Vi's target with a shield and a knock-up, turning her pick into a fight Vi's team did not choose. Teams picked Galio at 1.51x base rate after Vi and won 63.6% of 11 games.
tips: Draft Galio after Vi shows, and keep him in mid where his ultimate can reach either side lane.
Ult the teammate Vi locks down rather than a healthy frontliner, so the knock-up interrupts her follow-up combo.
Pair Galio with a second diver such as Jarvan IV or Camille, so his ultimate also has an offensive target.

why: Milio's value is keeping his carry safe at range with shields and disengage. Xayah shortens that distance: paired with an engage support she roots targets on the feather recall before Milio can kick anyone away, and Featherstorm lets her dodge the return engage. This is an older-meta pattern, picked at 1.93x base rate in 11 games with a 63.6% win rate.
tips: Pair Xayah with Rakan or another hard-engage support, since she needs someone to hold Milio's lane in place.
Place feathers behind Milio's carry before the engage starts, so the root is ready when the support commits.
Re-engage after Milio spends his kick, because his second disengage is much weaker.

why: Lee Sin's early game runs on landing Resonating Strike and choosing when to take the second dash. Twisted Fate's gold card is a point-and-click stun that removes that choice, and Destiny reveals Lee Sin's pathing before he can set up a play. Teams picked Twisted Fate at 2.51x base rate after Lee Sin across 11 games, winning 54.5% of them.
tips: Hold a locked gold card when Lee Sin's dash is available, instead of throwing it on cooldown.
Use Destiny before Lee Sin reaches an objective, so his flank and kick angles are visible to everyone.
Pair Twisted Fate with a jungler who can act on the stun immediately, such as Xin Zhao or Pantheon.

why: Cassiopeia needs time: her damage ramps as poison and twin fangs stack on targets who stay in range. Rell denies her that time by starting the fight instantly with Crash Down and Magnet Storm, before Cassiopeia can set her zone. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.91x base rate in 11 games but won only 27.3%, so teams kept drafting the engage idea without it paying off.
tips: Engage from fog or flank angles, because a front-facing Crash Down gives Cassiopeia time to ground and kite.
Pair Rell with burst damage that lands during Magnet Storm, before Cassiopeia's damage ramps.
Avoid long objective dances where Cassiopeia poisons the area first; force the fight or reset it.

why: Nocturne picks one target, turns out the lights, and fears them if they flee. Ahri is a poor target for that plan: Charm stops his dive mid-flight, and Spirit Rush gives her three dashes to break the fear tether and reposition. Teams picked her at 1.82x base rate after Nocturne and won 70% of 10 games, the best Nocturne answer by results.
tips: Save Charm for Nocturne's arrival instead of fishing with it while Paranoia is available.
Keep one Spirit Rush charge in reserve to break the fear tether rather than spending all three to engage.
Play Ahri mid with pushing power so Nocturne's jungler cannot roam freely between ultimates.

why: Bard's strength is leaving lane: his chimes and portals let him roam while his carry farms safely. Caitlyn punishes an absent support harder than most carries, shoving the wave with Piltover Peacemaker and zoning the stranded enemy with traps. Teams picked her at 1.63x base rate after Bard across 10 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Shove every wave Bard leaves, and place traps on the tower line to take plates during his roams.
Pair Caitlyn with a support who can hold lane alone briefly, such as Karma or Lux, without dying to Bard's return.
Ward Bard's portal exits near mid, so his roam timing becomes information instead of a surprise.

why: Orianna wants to scale in mid, control a zone with her ball, and decide teamfights with Shockwave. Renekton attacks her from the side lane instead: he takes the split-push she cannot match, then flanks and dives her in fights before she can layer her zone. Teams picked him at 1.58x base rate after Orianna in 10 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Send Renekton to the side lane Orianna would farm, and force her team to answer him before objectives.
Flank from fog in teamfights rather than walking at Orianna through her ball zone.
Pair Renekton with a mid laner who holds Orianna in lane, so she cannot follow his roams for free.

why: Seraphine's draft value is her ultimate: a long, charming wave that starts or flips a grouped fight. Sylas steals exactly that. Hijack turns Encore against Seraphine's own team, and his mobility lets him reach her backline position to do it. Teams picked Sylas at 2.6x base rate after Seraphine, though he won only 40% of 10 games, so the stolen ultimate alone has not decided the matchup.
tips: Steal Encore before an objective fight and hold it for Seraphine's team grouping, not for a single pick.
Pair Sylas with a jungler who can follow his engage while the stolen charm holds targets.
Take fights in open areas where a stolen Encore can hit multiple targets, rather than narrow chokes Seraphine controls.

why: Against Nocturne's point-and-click dive, Akali offers a target who can disappear: Twilight Shroud drops her from view as he lands, and her dashes break his fear tether. That is the draft idea behind a 1.77x lift, but it won only 30% of 10 games, since Akali still has to survive Paranoia's opening burst without a support's help.
tips: Drop the shroud as Nocturne lands rather than before, so its duration covers his fear and burst.
Keep Akali's second ultimate charge to leave the fight Nocturne started, not to chase a kill.
Pair Akali with a support or jungler who can shield her through the first moment of the dive.

why: Xayah's lane threatens a root whenever feathers line up behind her target. Milio extends his carry's range and shields the root's burst, then kicks Xayah's support away before the follow-up lands. Teams picked him at 1.85x base rate after Xayah, but won only 30% of 10 games, so the protective answer has underperformed the all-in answers to Xayah.
tips: Pair Milio with a long-range carry such as Caitlyn or Ashe, who can farm outside feather range entirely.
Spend the kick on Xayah's engage support, not on Xayah, so her feathers never get a held target.
Give up lane priority early and scale, rather than contesting Xayah's level-six all-in.

why: Cassiopeia focuses one poisoned target at a time, usually whoever dives or fronts for her opponents. Shen answers from another lane: Stand United shields that target through her burst, then his taunt pulls her off it. The idea lifted Shen to 2.09x base rate after Cassiopeia, but it won only 20% of 10 games, the weakest results in this set.
tips: Ult the teammate Cassiopeia is poisoning, not the healthiest ally, so the shield absorbs her focused damage.
Keep Shen in a side lane Cassiopeia cannot answer, so his ultimate is a numbers advantage rather than a rescue.
Taunt Cassiopeia herself on arrival when she has no Flash, since she has no dash to leave.

why: Yunara and Lulu form a protected hypercarry lane: Lulu shields and speeds Yunara while she stacks attacks. Kalista and Renata Glasc refuse the long trade entirely, threatening an early all-in with Fate's Call and Bailout that can kill before Yunara's steroid stacks. Teams picked the duo at 1.66x base rate after Yunara and Lulu, winning 66.7% of 9 games.
tips: Draft Kalista and Renata together after Yunara and Lulu show, and play for the level-two and level-six all-ins.
Throw Renata with Fate's Call to start fights, so Yunara cannot choose when to activate her steroid.
Stack spears on the target Lulu is not shielding, and switch the moment Polymorph is spent.

why: Shen wants a melee lane where he can taunt, block attacks, and then leave with Stand United. Corki never gives him that lane: he out-ranges Shen, pokes him down with rockets, and shoves waves Shen clears slowly. Teams picked Corki at 1.93x base rate after Shen across 9 games, winning 55.6% of them.
tips: Poke Shen from max range and keep the wave shoved, so he must choose between farm and his ultimate.
Call out every Shen ultimate immediately, since Corki cannot follow it and must trade farm or plates instead.
Keep Corki's Valkyrie for Shen's taunt dash rather than using it to join fights early.

why: Ezreal's safety comes from Arcane Shift: he blinks away from danger and pokes from range. Twisted Fate removes the guesswork, because Destiny reveals where Ezreal repositions and a locked gold card holds him for his team. Teams picked Twisted Fate at 1.81x base rate after Ezreal in 9 games, winning 55.6% of them.
tips: Use Destiny as Ezreal steps up to poke, so his blink direction is known before the gold card flies.
Pair Twisted Fate with a jungler who can reach Ezreal during the stun, such as Xin Zhao or Vi.
Push mid and roam rather than trading poke with Ezreal, who wins a passive farming lane.

why: Ashe and Seraphine control a lane with slows, poke, and two long-range ultimates that start fights from safety. Zeri and Yuumi concede that early control on purpose: Yuumi keeps Zeri healthy through the poke, and once Zeri scales her mobility and area damage outrun a lane built on landing skillshots. The pair spiked to 8.78x base rate after Ashe and Seraphine, the highest lift in the set, across 9 games at 44.4% wins.
tips: Draft Zeri and Yuumi only with a team that can survive the first fifteen minutes without bot lane priority.
Stay behind the wave and give plates rather than trading into Ashe and Seraphine's poke at low health.
Pair the lane with a scaling mid or top laner, so the game plan does not depend on winning bot lane early.

why: Kalista's lane hops around skillshots and stacks spears for Rend executes, which makes her hard to lock down in a fair fight. Neeko attacks that mobility directly: she approaches disguised as a minion or ally, roots through the wave, and bursts before Kalista can hop away. Teams picked Neeko at 4.84x base rate after Kalista in 9 games, winning 44.4% of them.
tips: Use Neeko's disguise on every approach, since a visible Neeko never reaches a hopping Kalista.
Root through the minion wave as Kalista hops forward to stack spears, not while she retreats.
Pair Neeko with a carry who follows her root instantly, such as Lucian or Samira.

why: Qiyana's jungle and mid dives delete one target with her river or wall ultimate before they can respond. Lulu is the standard answer to single-target burst: Polymorph stops Qiyana mid-combo, and Wild Growth plus her shield keep the target alive through it. Teams picked Lulu at 1.7x base rate after Qiyana across 9 games, winning 44.4% of them.
tips: Hold Polymorph for Qiyana's dive rather than spending it on poke, even if that means a quieter lane.
Stand the carry near walls Qiyana cannot use, and ward river entrances before objectives.
Pair Lulu with a carry who can keep fighting after Wild Growth, such as Yunara or Kog'Maw.

why: Camille's Hextech Ultimatum traps one carry in a cage with no exit. Skarner is one of the few answers that works inside that moment: Impale drags Camille away from her target, and his durability survives her true-damage burst. Teams picked Skarner at 1.84x base rate after Camille in 9 games, winning 44.4% of them.
tips: Keep Skarner near the carry Camille will trap, instead of engaging first and leaving her free.
Drag Camille toward your team with Impale, not away from the fight, so the cage time becomes her danger.
Track Camille's ultimate cooldown and force fights while it is down, when she cannot isolate anyone.

why: Lee Sin wants early skirmishes, invades, and snowballing lanes before he falls off. Yorick refuses that game from top lane: he splits, takes towers with his ghouls and the Maiden, and forces Lee Sin's team to answer him instead of fighting. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.51x base rate in 9 games, winning 44.4% of them.
tips: Send Yorick to the lane farthest from the next objective, so Lee Sin's team must split to answer him.
Keep the Maiden alive through the early game; without it Yorick cannot threaten towers alone.
Pair Yorick with a team that can stall at objectives without fighting, such as a poke mid and a disengage support.

why: Ashe's ultimate is a global pick tool that lets her team start fights from a screen away. Sylas steals it and uses it the same way, while his dashes let him reach Ashe herself, an immobile carry with no escape once caught. Teams picked Sylas at 2.86x base rate after Ashe across 9 games, though he won only 33.3%, so the stolen arrow has been stronger in theory than in results.
tips: Steal Ashe's arrow before objective setups and fire it down the lane her team must walk through.
Use Sylas's dashes on Ashe after she spends her arrow, when she has no way to create distance.
Pair Sylas with a jungler who can follow a long-range arrow instantly, such as Vi or Jarvan IV.

why: Ashe and Seraphine together offer two fight-starting ultimates and a lane full of slows. Sylas can steal either one: Ashe's arrow for a pick, or Seraphine's Encore for a grouped engage, and his mobility reaches the immobile pair behind their poke. Teams picked him at 3.14x base rate against the duo, winning 33.3% of 9 games.
tips: Choose the stolen ultimate by the fight shape: arrow for a pick, Encore when both teams group.
Dive the Ashe or Seraphine who just spent her ultimate, since neither has a dash to escape.
Pair Sylas with hard engage from jungle or support, so a stolen ultimate has immediate follow-up.

why: Ezreal and Karma poke from range and never have to commit. Lucian and Milio answer by committing anyway: Milio's shields and speed let Lucian dash in, burst, and survive the return poke, flipping a poke lane into repeated all-ins. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.62x base rate in 9 games but won only 11.1%, the worst results in the set, so the all-in idea has largely failed against the poke lane.
tips: Trade only when Milio's shield and kick are both ready, so Lucian can leave after his burst.
Pair the lane with a jungler who ganks early, because Lucian and Milio cannot win by farming against poke.
Avoid this answer if the enemy adds more disengage; one more peel tool leaves Lucian stranded after his dash.

why: Ambessa dives the backline with chained dashes and locks a carry with her ultimate. Kai'Sa is one of the few carries who can answer a dive herself: Killer Instinct repositions her with a shield, and her evolved invisibility drops Ambessa's target lock mid-combo. Teams picked Kai'Sa at 1.64x base rate after Ambessa and won 87.5% of 8 games, the best win rate in this set.
tips: Hold Kai'Sa's ultimate until Ambessa commits hers, then dash to plasma-marked frontline rather than away alone.
Use the invisibility to break Ambessa's chase between her dashes, not to re-enter immediately.
Pair Kai'Sa with a support who can mark targets and peel the second diver, such as Nautilus or Renata Glasc.

why: Gnar's teamfight depends on arriving as Mega Gnar and stunning a grouped team against a wall. Sylas steals that exact ultimate and can use it without managing rage, while his dashes and healing sustain through Mini Gnar's poke. Teams picked Sylas at 2.18x base rate after Gnar and won 75% of 8 games.
tips: Steal Gnar's ultimate only when he is in Mega form and a fight is near, since the stolen version needs a wall nearby.
Fight away from walls when Sylas holds the stolen ultimate, and near them when he does not.
Pair Sylas with a top laner who pressures Mini Gnar in lane, so Gnar reaches fights behind on items.

why: Yunara must stand still at high attack speed to do her damage, and she has no hard escape when a diver arrives. Qiyana exploits that: she crosses the river or a wall with her ultimate and deletes Yunara before her steroid stacks. Teams picked Qiyana at 1.63x base rate after Yunara, winning 62.5% of 8 games.
tips: Draft Qiyana in jungle or mid with a lane that gives her river access, where her ultimate is strongest.
Dive Yunara as she activates her attack-speed steroid, when she is committed to standing and attacking.
Pair Qiyana with a support who can shield her exit, since she has no way out after the kill attempt.

why: Cassiopeia punishes champions who walk at her slowly, stacking poison while they close. Leona closes instantly instead, chaining Zenith Blade and her stuns so Cassiopeia is locked before her damage ramps. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.53x base rate in 8 games and won 62.5% of them.
tips: Engage Cassiopeia from fog or behind her wave, so she cannot poison the approach path first.
Chain Leona's stuns without gaps, because one free second lets Cassiopeia ground and kite.
Pair Leona with a burst carry or mid laner who kills Cassiopeia inside the stun chain.

why: Ashe wins lane with range, slows, and poke that immobile enchanters struggle to answer. Yuumi sidesteps that lane entirely by attaching to a scaling partner: her heals erase Ashe's poke over time, and late game the attached pair out-values Ashe's utility. Teams picked Yuumi at 6.27x base rate after Ashe across 8 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Attach Yuumi to the most mobile scaler on the team, not automatically to the bot laner.
Give up early lane pressure and plates rather than trading into Ashe's slows at low health.
Detach only to block an Ashe arrow or proc Yuumi's shield, then reattach before the follow-up lands.

why: Nocturne dives a chosen target through Paranoia and fears them if they run. Locke is a target who can fight the dive instead: Soul Ignition stores the damage he takes as grey health and converts it into healing, and his resetting dash lets him chase or leave once the fear ends. Teams picked Locke at 1.57x base rate after Nocturne across 8 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Activate Soul Ignition as Nocturne lands, so his opening burst becomes Locke's healing pool.
Keep Locke's dash reset for the moment the fear ends, rather than spending it to engage during Paranoia.
Pair Locke with a support who can see targets during Paranoia, such as one with a shield or reveal.

why: Nocturne's dive isolates one target while the lights are out. Leona makes that isolation expensive: she is durable enough to survive being the target, and her stun chain holds Nocturne for the counter-engage when vision returns. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.55x base rate in 8 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Keep Leona beside the carry Nocturne will dive, not at the front starting fights, while Paranoia is ready.
Stun Nocturne on landing and save the second crowd control for when his spell shield is spent.
Pair Leona with a carry who can turn and burst Nocturne during her stun chain, such as Samira or Lucian.

why: Varus controls lane with long-range poke and locks targets with Chain of Corruption. Leona refuses the poke lane by engaging through it: Zenith Blade reaches Varus past his range advantage, and her stun chain holds an immobile carry with no dash. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.92x base rate in 8 games, splitting them at 50% wins.
tips: Engage when Varus steps up to charge his arrow, since he is slowed and stationary while charging.
Pair Leona with an early-game carry such as Lucian or Draven who converts her stuns into kills.
Ward the river before engaging, because Varus's team will counter-gank a committed Leona with no exit.

why: Akali dives, hides in her shroud, and leaves when the fight turns. Renekton's empowered stun is point-and-click, so it catches her without needing to find her in the shroud, and his early lane strength denies her the farm she needs to dive anyone. Teams picked Renekton at 2.38x base rate after Akali, though he won only 37.5% of 8 games.
tips: Spend Renekton's empowered stun only on Akali, even if another target is lower, while her shroud is available.
Push Akali under her tower early so she must spend energy on farm instead of roams.
Keep Renekton in the side lane Akali wants to split, so she cannot avoid him all game.

why: Qiyana deletes a target against a wall or in the river before they can react. Ahri answers with Charm, which stops her dive mid-dash, and Spirit Rush, which moves Ahri away from the wall Qiyana needs. This older-meta answer appeared at 1.98x base rate in 8 games, winning 37.5% of them.
tips: Hold Charm for Qiyana's dash rather than throwing it at her while she holds her ultimate.
Fight away from walls and river edges when Ahri's ultimate is on cooldown.
Push mid and move first, so Qiyana's jungler or mid laner cannot roam to side lanes freely.
